text.p: - The Swiss government decided on Wedensday that Switzerland should take part in NATO's Partnership for Peace under the condition Switzerland's neutrality will not be affected.

- Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro will visit Switzerland between the 11th and the 13th of September. He will first meet all members of the Swiss government in Berne and then visit the cantons of Vaud and Ticino.
- A federal commission for security reaffirmed its decision to ban the export of Pilatus training jets only to countries that fall under an international embargo.
- Swissair subsidy to take over Danish information technology group Plus Data Gruppen. The Danish company, which is a leader in transportation software applications, employs 70 people.

- Swiss authorities introduced a new service on the internet. Under the web address http://www.admin.ch/bfs, users will find information fed by the Swiss Office for Statistics. Divided into 20 sections, the service mainly provides data of every day life.
- Swiss machine group Maag reported a 2 million Swiss francs net profit for the 1996 first half. During the same period last year it lost 19 million francs.
- Pierre-Alain Blum resigned from his job as CEO for the Swiss watch manufacturer Ebel.
- Some 400 young Swiss men have so far applied to do civil service instead of going to the army. Switzlerland will introduce a civil service as an alternative to the army on October 1.
